writeup: TIC 140918728 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.8221 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse that dims the system by 1.68 percent, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 230.0 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 59.1, though the centroid offset measures 3.3 arcseconds from the nominal position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it potentially novel. The machine learning classifier assigned it a score of 0.42, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a real eclipsing binary system.
